character: Family-owned mid-sized ski area about 20 road miles east of Ithaca and the largest in Central New York, with roughly 950 ft (290 m) of vertical spread over several ridges and lit terrain for night skiing. The base has a slopeside hotel (Hope Lake Lodge) with an indoor waterpark, plus snow tubing and Nordic trails.
learning: Beginners buy a Beginner Area Pass that covers the gentle learning slopes and Chair #3, a beginner chairlift. The resort lists two magic carpets. The Learning Center teaches first-timers at stations using Terrain Based Learning, where shaped snow features control speed. The 'Intro2Snow' package is for never-evers aged 7 and up. Group and private lessons run 1.5 h or 3 h, starting at 10am, noon, 2pm and 4pm. Kids can join Kidz World (Mountain Minis and Trail Blazers) or the 8-week Mountaineers Club (ages 7-14). Cornell, SUNY Cortland and TC3 run college PE ski/snowboard courses here. In school and PE programs an Ability Card system limits which lifts students may ride, and Chair 3 is the only lift allowed without a card. Children 6 and under ski free.

source.note: Opened Black Friday; more trails added Dec 5-6, 2025. Season wound down late March with pond skimming Sat Apr 4, 2026; exact closing date not captured.

season.typicalText: Usually starts around Thanksgiving weekend to early December, weather and snowmaking permitting (NYSkiBlog). Opened Fri Nov 28, 2025 (Black Friday) and Thu Dec 5, 2024; the 2023-24 season started around Dec 21, 2023 (WBNG). Seasons ran about 108 days (2024-25) and 114 days (2025-26).
season.notes: No resort-announced 2026-27 opening or closing date found as of 2026-09-28. OnTheSnow (third party) projects 2026-11-27 to 2027-03-28 (~113 days); that is a projection, not an announcement (https://www.onthesnow.com/new-york/greek-peak/ski-resort). For 2026-27 the resort fast-tracked a $3M 'Greek Peak East' snowmaking project (announced 2026-03-20), compressing a four-year plan into one off-season: about 250 HKD semi-automated snow guns, ~33,000 ft of new pipe and a 450 hp pump (~+20% water capacity), extending snowmaking to east-side trails including the double-black Olympian (https://www.iskiny.com/news/greek-peak-mountain-resort-accelerate-current-four-year-snow-making-plan-one-year, https://unofficialnetworks.com/2026/08/24/greek-peak-olympian-snowmaking/). In 2025-26 all lift tickets had to be bought online before arrival (no ticket windows).

driveFromIthaca.basis: Rome2rio: about 19.7 road miles and ~33 min from Ithaca to Greek Peak Mountain Resort (Ultimate-Ski gives ~22 mi / 30 min). Typical route: NY-13 toward Cortland, then NY-392.

transfers.name: OurBus Ithaca - Greek Peak Ski Resort
transfers.notes: Leaves Downtown Ithaca (E. Seneca St, in front of Ithaca Deli) and stops at the shuttle stop in front of Greek Peak's main lodge. Fares were advertised from $10; schedules are seasonal. Researched — confirm current schedule.

transfers.name: Cornell Ski & Snowboard Club weekend bus
transfers.notes: Free for club members (membership about $30/yr). Runs Cornell to Greek Peak on about six winter weekends, stopping at North Campus, West Campus and Collegetown. A free weekly OurBus also ran on Monday College Night. Researched — confirm for 2026-27.

conflicts: Summit elevation: 2,100 ft (Indy Pass, NYSkiBlog, other directories) vs 2,200 ft / 670 m (Wikipedia). Base 1,148 ft + 952 ft vertical = 2,100 ft, so 2,100 was used.

Lift count: 8 (Indy Pass, NYSkiBlog: quad, 3 doubles, triple, beginner double, 2 carpets) vs 9 lifts (SANY listing) vs '6 chairlifts, 2 magic carpets, 1 tubing carpet' (Wikipedia). 8 skier lifts were used.
Trail count: 55 (Wikipedia, Indy) vs 56 trails and glades (SANY listing).
Snowmaking coverage: about 83% (search summary citing Wikipedia/OnTheSnow) vs 80% of 220 acres (NYSkiBlog). 83 was used. The 2026 Greek Peak East project should raise coverage.
Terrain parks: 3 terrain-park trails (Wikipedia breakdown) vs 4 terrain parks (NYSkiBlog). 3 was used.
Difficulty %: computed from the Wikipedia trail breakdown (20 easier, 16 more difficult, 14 most difficult, 5 expert = 55). Advanced = most difficult + expert.

Season-pass price ladder: search summaries repeatedly state '2026-27 passes on sale for $635 through March 1; $699 Mar 2-31; $799 Apr 1-Sep 30; $999 after Oct 1'. But the '$635, up to $799 April 1' wording traces to a Binghamton Homepage article of 2025-03-19 (2025-26 passes). A Greek Peak Facebook post also advertised 2025-26 passes at $535. Only $799/$999 are attributed to the 2026/27 official page with confidence.

Adult day ticket: 'around $120' (Greek Peak's own pass marketing) vs $94 (OnTheSnow) vs $65-$89 depending on date (SnowStash) vs $92 ski-club rate (Onondaga Ski Club, 2025-26). Prices are dynamic and online-only.
3-day ticket: $249 (about $83/day) per search summary vs '$77/day' in the Greek Peak blog post 'Three Days, Infinite Thrills' (possibly a different season or sale).

Night-skiing hours: official lift-ticket page says '3:30 PM to close'. One unattributed search summary gave Mon-Fri 9:30-16:00, Sat 8:30-16:00 and night Mon-Sat 15:30-21:00. skiresort.info lists floodlit times of Mon-Thu 16:00-18:00 and Fri-Sat from 17:00. Only the official and WBNG-sourced times were recorded.
2025-26 opening: SnowStash listed a scheduled opening of Dec 13, 2025 (pre-season). The actual opening was Black Friday, Nov 28, 2025 (WBNG, CNYCentral).
research.confidenceNotes: WebFetch was blocked, so facts come from web-search result summaries; greekpeak.net pages could not be read directly. High confidence: vertical and base elevation, trail count, location, Indy partnership, 2025-26 and 2024-25 opening dates, the snowmaking project. Medium: hours and 2025-26 ticket prices. Low: snowmaking %, lift count and terrain-park count (vary by source). The summit weather point is an unsourced approximation for weather-model use only. links.interactiveMap is a third-party map (SteepSeeker), not an official one. Season passes are catalogued in passes.json, not here.
